name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Crawford seeking re-election with large cash advantage
Democratic challenger raised only $65k with minimal cash on hand
model.rationale: Crawford holds a heavily Republican seat with a million-dollar war chest against a minimally funded challenger, and markets price the race at roughly 98% Republican. The fundamentals baseline of about a 20-point Republican margin fits comfortably.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Crawford's primary fallout shifting general-election dynamics is the only realistic path to movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: This northeastern Arkansas seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of about 23 points toward the GOP. Rick Crawford, the incumbent since 2011, is running for another term and has built a substantial financial advantage, with roughly $1 million on hand. His Democratic challenger, Terri Green, has raised only about $65,000 and has minimal cash available, leaving her little capacity to compete. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race rests on fundamentals, all of which point the same direction. Crawford is a heavy favorite, and the contest is rated Safe Republican.
